1. Vide this judgment, I propose to dispose of the present appeal filed by the appellants against the impugned order dated 24.02.2020, whereby the Ld. Adjudicating Officer, imposed penalty under Section 52 Sandeep Wasuja Ors. Vs. FSO of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 (in short "the FSS Act") and Rules, 2011 & Regulations, 2011, along with Section 23, Section 26(1), Section 26(2(ii)
of FSS Act read with Section 3(1)(zf) of FSS Act.

The Adjudicating Officer also found the appellants to have violated Regulation No. 2.2.2.10 & 2.3.2.1(a) of the Food Safety & Standards (Packaging &
Labelling) Regulation, 2011 (in short "the FSS (P&L) Regulation").
The Adjudicating Officer also concluded that the sample gave false declaration regarding composition of food in contravention of Section 3(1)(d) and 24(2)(a) of FSS Act.
The Adjudicating Officer vide the impugned order imposed a penalty of Rs.80,000/ each upon the appellants namely Sh. Sandeep Wasuja, Sh. Ajay Mugrai and Mrs. Veena Mugrai.

2. In backdrop, Sh. Tarun Negi, Food Safety Officer had filed an application under Rule 3.1.1(3) of FSS Rules, 2011 before the Adjudicating Officer alleging therein that on 01.03.2019, a sample of "Marori" for analysis was taken from the appellant Sh. Sandeep Wasuja S/o Sh. Gopal Krishan Wasuja, Food Business Operator (in short "FBO") of M/s Bikaner Namkeen Sandeep Wasuja Ors.
Vs. FSO Wala, GR5, Plot No. 5, Krit Plaza, LSC Market, Surajmal Vihar, Delhi110 092.

sentences.text: Each counterpart of the said sample were separately marked, fastened up and sealed according to the Food Safety Act / Rules & Regulations.
Sh. Ajay Kumar Yadav, also joined the said proceedings as an independent witness.
Notice in Form VA was prepared on the spot and the copy of the same was given to the appellant Sh. Sandeep Wasuja and the price of Rs.240/ was paid to him vide receipt dated 01.03.2019.
The necessary documents were prepared.
3. The sample was sent to the Food Analyst, for analysis on 05.03.2019.
The FBO did not request to send the fourth part of the sample for analysis from an NABL accredited Laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011.

The Food Analyst vide his report no.
FSS/296/2019 dated 14.03.2019 has reported and opined that the sample is misbranded because there was violation of Regulation No. 2.2.2.10 & 2.3.2.1(a) of the FSS (P&L) Regulation, 2011.

The Food Analyst also opined that the sample gave false declaration regarding Sandeep Wasuja Ors. Vs.
FSO composition of food in contravention of section 3(1)(d) and 24(2)(a) of FSS Act, 2006, because it does not declare 'Added vegetable oil' as one of the ingredients, although, it is present in the sample in considerable amount.

sentences.text: The Food Analyst had further stated in his report that the 'Best Before not declared in capital letters' as per the requirement of Regulation no. 2.2.2.10 of the FSS (P&L) Regulation, 2011.

The Food Analyst had also stated in his report that the area of principal display panel (5x5cm = 25 sq. cm) of the rectangular package is only 6.29% of the area of the panel of the package having largest area (22.3 x 17.8cm = 396.94 sq. cm.), which shall not be less than 40%.
4. The FBO did not exercise his right to file an appeal against the report of Food Analyst.

In the complaint, it was stated that appellant no.2 Sh. Ajay Mugrai is the proprietor of M/s Bikaner Namkeen Wala and looking after its daytoday business and as such, he is in charge of and responsible for the conduct of the business of the said firm.
5. It was further stated that the sampled article of food "Marori" was manufactured by M/s Amar Bakery, Sandeep Wasuja Ors.
Vs. FSO 531, Bada Bazaar, Shahdara, Delhi110032.

Appellant no.3 Mrs. Veena Mugrai is the sole proprietor of M/s Amar Bakery and looking after its daytoday business and as such, she is in charge of and responsible for the conduct of the business of the said firm.

6. In the proceedings before the Adjudicating Officer, the appellants stated that the label was printed by their staff under the lack of knowledge of the respective labelling rules and they have made the necessary changes in the label as per the FSS (P&L) Regulation, 2011.

The Adjudicating Officer vide the impugned order after recording the facts and submissions of the appellants reproduce Sections 23, 26(1)&(2), 3(1)(d) and 3(1)(zf) of the FSS Act, inter alia holding that he is of the considered view to impose a penalty under Section 52 of the FSS Act and Rules, 2011 &
Regulations, 2011, along with Section 23, Section 26(1), Section 26(2(ii) of FSS Act read with Section 3(1)(zf) of FSS Act.

The Adjudicating Officer also found the appellants to have violated Regulation No. 2.2.2.10 & 2.3.2.1(a) of the Food Safety & Standards (Packaging & Labelling) Regulation, 2011 (in short "the FSS (P&L) Regulation").

sentences.text: The Adjudicating Officer vide the impugned order imposed a penalty of Rs.80,000/ each upon the appellants namely Sh. Sandeep Wasuja, Sh. Ajay Mugrai and Mrs. Veena Mugrai.
7. The appellants have challenged the impugned order on the ground that the sample confirms to the standards and it was only found misbranded.
The appellants further stated that the 'best before not' was written in capital letters.
It has further been submitted that merely on this violation, the appellants could not have been punished by the Adjudicating Officer.
The appellants have further stated that no document has been filed by the complainant to show that appellant nos.2&3 were responsible for the conduct of the business of the firm.
It has been submitted that impugned order is liable to be set aside.
The appellants have further stated that in law, no standard has been prescribed for the seized article.

It has been submitted that in the complaint filed before the Adjudicating Officer or the Adjudicating Officer in the impugned order has not mentioned about any standard Sandeep Wasuja Ors. Vs. FSO fixed by the law for the sample taken.

8. In respect of appellant nos.2&3, Ld. Counsel submitted that the department has not produced even an iota of evidence that they were looking after the affairs of the said firm or were responsible in any manner.

Counsel for the appellants has submitted that in M.D. Anand Aqua (Supra),
the Hon'ble High Court of Patna inter alia held that the bottled drinking water was found misbranded as it did not mention "BEST BEFORE" in capital letters, rather it was printed in small Sandeep Wasuja Ors.
Vs. FSO letters.

Counsel for the appellants has further submitted that in Oscar Josheph (Supra), the Hon'ble Jharkahand High Court inter alia held that there was sufficient compliance of Rule 32 even if the words "Best before three months" were not written in the bold letter over the packets as required under Rule 32, however, it was written in small letters..

Ld. Counsel for the appellants has submitted that in Ram Kishan Rohtagi (Supra),
the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that in respect of the Directors of the company are concerned, there was not even a whisper nor a shred of evidence nor anything to show, apart from the presumption drawn by the complainant that there is any act committed by the Directors from which a reasonable inference can be drawn that they could also be vicariously liable.

13. It has been submitted that similarly, in the present case, there is not even an iota of evidence against appellant nos.2&3.
14.
Sh. Kundan Kohli, Ld. Chief PP for the State, in the brief synopsis, has fairly stated that the sample was Sandeep Wasuja Ors.

Vs. FSO found to be misbranded because there was violation of regulation no. 2.2.2.10 & 2.3.2.1(a) of FSS (P&L)
Regulations, which are reproduced as under :
"a). the sample gave false declaration regarding composition of food in contravention of Section 3(1)(d) and 24(2)(a) of FSS Act, because it does not declare 'Added vegetable oil' as one of the ingredients, although, it is present in the sample in considerable amount;
b).

The Food Analyst has stated regarding label that the 'Best Before not declared in capital letters' as per the requirement of Regulation no. 2.2.2.10 of the FSS (P&L)
Regulation, 2011 &
c).

he area of principal display panel (5x5cm = 25 sq. cm) of the rectangular package is only 6.29% of the area of the panel of the package having largest area (22.3 x 17.8cm = 396.94 sq. cm.), which shall not be less than 40%.
This is violation of Rule 2.3.2. of FSS (P&L) Regulation, 2011."
Sandeep Wasuja Ors. Vs. FSO 15.
I have heard the submissions of both the parties and perused the record carefully.
16. I consider that the impugned order dated 24.02.2020 cannot sustain in the eyes of law and liable to be set aside for reasons more than one.
The entire reading of the impugned order makes it clear that the Adjudicating Officer has not applied his mind at all.

The reading of the impugned order would make it clear that the Adjudicating Officer simply recorded the facts and thereafter, recorded the contentions of the respondent/ appellants herein in a very casual manner and finally gave his finding regarding the guilt of the appellants and have ordered punishment.
The Adjudicating Officer should not have exercised his jurisdiction in such a manner.
The order of the Adjudicating Officer seems to have been passed without any application of mind.
It does not have any reason.
The proceedings before the Adjudicating Officer is quasi judicial in nature.
The Adjudicating Officer was bound to give reasons for arriving at a particular conclusion.

I consider that merely on this ground,
the proceedings before the Adjudicating Officer should be set aside.

sentences.text: It is also pertinent to mention herein that as far Sandeep Wasuja Ors.

Vs. FSO as the offence pertaining to misbranding is concerned, it has repeatedly been held that even if the label printing on the food article regarding date of manufacturing and expiry was mentioned in the small letters, it is sufficient compliance of the provision.

In respect of the other report of the Food Analyst that the said sample did not declare 'Added vegetable oil' as one of the ingredients, although, it is present in the sample in considerable amount, is concerned, the record would reveal that no standard has been mentioned in the entire case.
Thus, case of the department is also liable to failed on this count.
18. In view of the discussions made hereinabove, the appeal is allowed.
19. Record of the Adjudicating Officer be returned along with copy of the judgment.
20. Appeal file be consigned to Record Room.
